**Analysis of the microscopic image:**

**Affected structure:** This is a microscopy image (100 µm scale bar), showing fungal/oomycete reproductive structures — not a macroscopic plant part.

**Key visual features:**
- Large, ovoid to lemon-shaped sporangia (~30–50 µm in length based on scale bar)
- Borne singly at the tips of long, slender, hyaline (transparent), curved sporangiophores
- The sporangiophores show characteristic swellings/nodes at branching points
- Sporangia are uninucleate-appearing, granular, and translucent/grey-green
- Classic sympodial branching pattern of the sporangiophore

**Reasoning:**
These structures are unmistakably the sporangia and sporangiophores of **Phytophthora infestans**, the causal agent of **Late Blight**. The diagnostic features — lemon/ovoid-shaped large sporangia, borne on long branching sympodial sporangiophores with distinctive swellings at branching nodes — are the textbook microscopic signature of this oomycete. No other class on the list produces sporangia of this morphology: Early Blight (*Alternaria*) has club-shaped, multi-septate conidia; Gray Mold (*Botrytis*) has small rounded conidia in clusters; Septoria produces filiform conidia in pycnidia; Powdery Mildew has barrel-shaped conidia in chains.
